chunks: And with the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi, from Abu Hafs al-Attar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon them both) narrating from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

Jibreel came to me at an hour he had never come before, and on a day he had never come before. So I said to him: O Jibreel, you have come to me at an hour and day you never used to come. You have terrified me!
He said: What frightens you, O Muhammad, when God has already forgiven you your past and future lapses?
He said: Then what message has your Lord sent you with? He said: Your Lord forbids you from worshipping idols, drinking intoxicants, and vilifying people.
And there is one more thing, important for the hereafter and this life: your Lord says to you: O Muhammad, I have never detested any container as much as I detest a full stomach.

key_terms.الخمور: Intoxicants (khumoor) -- all forms of alcoholic drinks
key_terms.ملاحاة: Vilifying, quarreling, or engaging in hostile verbal altercation
key_terms.وعاء: Container or vessel -- used here metaphorically for the stomach

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about overeating and a full stomach in Islam?
ai.summary: In this prophetic hadith from al-Amali of al-Mufid, the Prophet (SAWW) recounts an extraordinary visit from the angel Jibreel at an unusual time, which alarmed him. Jibreel reassured him by reminding him of God's forgiveness, then conveyed four divine prohibitions: idol worship, consuming intoxicants, reviling others, and overeating. The final prohibition, expressed as God's intense dislike of a full stomach, underscores Islam's emphasis on moderation in eating as a spiritual discipline with consequences in both this world and the next.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 21. And with the first chain of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Hashami, from Abi Hafs al-Attar, who said, I heard Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, relating from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:
Once Jibraeel came to me at an unusual hour and on an unusual day. So, I told him: "O Jibraeel, you have indeed come to me at an unusual hour and unusual day. You have struck me with awe!"
He said: "O Muhammad, you have no cause of fear, for Allah has forgiven you your past and future lapse."
I said: "Then what is the message (this time) from your Lord?" He said: "Your Lord forbids you to worship the idols and to drink any type of intoxicants and to vilify the people.
And there is one more (worth remembering) here and hereafter; your Lord says to you: O Muhammad, I have never felt indignation at any container as much as at a filled stomach."
